utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. The interpreters and the technicians are ready? Very well, thank you. After this very long break, we are now going to resume with our case. So will the registry please remind us of the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is number IT-95-14/1-T, the Prosecutor versus Zlatko Aleksovski. The office of the Prosecutor, will you please introduce yourself, although we all know each other very well?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, please, my name is Niemann. I appear with my colleague, Mr. Meddegoda and Ms. Sutherland for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: The Defence, Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Goran Mikulicic and, together with my co-counsel, Mr. Joka, we act on behalf of the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: All right. We have a day ahead of us and I believe the Prosecutor would like to present his next case. You have the floor, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, please, on the last occasion we indicated that our last witness, Professor Bianchini, wouldn't be available today and we endeavoured to see whether he could change that so he could be available today, but these appointments remain fixed, so he will be here tomorrow. Your Honours, Professor Bianchini was to introduce a large number of documents, which is a slow and time-consuming process, and if Your Honours, please, and if it is convenient to the court, it may be fruitful for us to introduce those exhibits today, then when Professor Bianchini comes tomorrow we can proceed with his evidence much more expeditiously rather than being delayed each time with the process of dealing with exhibits one by one. I have spoken to Mr. Mikulicic about this and he has kindly conceded to this procedure which will considerably increase the efficiency of this last witness in terms of exhibits. There's a lot of exhibits, unfortunately, Your Honour. What I thought I might do, is I will introduce them one by one and we can display them on the overhead projector so that they appear on Your Honours' screen and the screen of the Defence and I will just explain them one by one as we go through. Then tomorrow when Professor Bianchini seeks to refer to them, he can just refer to them as tendered exhibits. If that's a course that's convenient and acceptable to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, before that, let me first ask Mr. Mikulicic what his position is on this proposal made by Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as my esteemed colleague Mr. Niemann has said, before we started this discussion, we talked about this and the Defence has no reservations to this way of proceeding with the presentation of the case and the tendering of the exhibits to the file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Niemann. You may begin. Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic, I'm sorry. Mr. Niemann, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next exhibit in order that we would seek to tender, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next exhibit, Your Honours, that we would seek to tender, and I will place this on the overhead projector, relates to the ethnic composition of the Yugoslav People's Army prior to -- in 1989 and based on the 1981 statistics. I have a copy for Your Honours and a copy for the registrar and the copy that's on the screen I'll make available to Mr. Mikulicic. Mr. Mikulicic has originally -- should have all of these exhibits. We have provided to him these exhibits previously. If we could be told the exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be number 105.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next document is also -- Excuse me, Your Honours. Mr. Mikulicic has no objection, Your Honours, because he has seen these before. What I might to, if he doesn't mind, is display them on the screen and then hand them to him at the end of this process. It saves a lot of wandering around the courtroom. I don't know whether Mr. Mikulicic has objection to that, but it will appear on his screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Of course, the Defence agrees to this manner of case presentation, but it would certainly facilitate the work of the Defence if we were to get these documents in parallel so that the Defence could also mark, for its own sake, the exhibit numbers for its purposes so we could react more readily to these documents. If that is not too much of a problem, I would kindly ask that we proceed in this way, if it is at all possible, or perhaps if we could get these documents as a batch later, but they should be marked with the exhibit number which is the number of the exhibit in the file. That would facilitate work for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think it's better for Mr. Mikulicic to have his copy--.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I think that's a practical issue, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: --available to him as we progressively get through. The next document, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The JNA, the ethnic composition of the commands of the JNA before 1991, and it's now displayed on Your Honours' screen. I tender that and might it be given the next number in order?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be number 106.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours, is a map, which I now place on the screen, and this document shows the progressive creation of the Serb-autonomous regions in Bosnia-Herzegovina during the early part of 1991. I have a copy for Mr. Mikulicic and for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be number 107.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours, shows the results of a referendum held in Bosnia relating to the question of the Serb attitude towards the formation of an independent sovereign state of Bosnia-Herzegovina in February of 1991. I supply a copy of that for Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be number 108.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next document is a table and it relates to the respective sizes of the forces confronting each other in Bosnia-Herzegovina during the early part of the war in 1991. I have a copy for Mr. Mikulicic and for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 109.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours, is a map of Bosnia-Herzegovina showing the progressive development of the proclamation of the Croatia autonomous regions in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours, is a map also showing the areas not claimed by either the Bosnian Serbs or the Bosnian Croats, and disputed areas or areas which are claimed by both Bosnian Serbs and Bosnian Croats, again in the period 1991-1992. Tender that map, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 111.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours, is also a map. It's an historical map showing the State of Croatia or the "benate" of Croatia in 1939-1941. I tender that map, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 112.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next, Your Honour, is also a map, an historical map, showing the concept of Greater Serbia according to one Stefan Mihavic who had a project for the creation of Greater Serbia. I tender that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 113.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next map is also a map of Croatia and the Yugoslav State in 1918. I tender a copy of that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 114.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next map is a map showing the territory of Croatia during World War II. I tender that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number 115.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next, Your Honour, maps, is a series of maps which we wish to tender as a group, a group of maps, showing the ethnic division in Bosnia-Herzegovina between Muslims, Serbs, and Croats, and then the position with respect to Muslims, the cantonisation, and the state of the proclamation of the area of Krajina in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and if they could be numbered the next exhibit number in order, "A" through to "E"? So I think it would be 116 "A" through "E."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, this is number 116 from "A" to "E."

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm missing one copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next document is an anagram which shows the structure of the HV-HVO in the periods 1991-92. I tender that exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is number 117.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next is a document that appears both in the Croatian and the English language, English translation of it. It's the conclusions of a meeting of the community of Herzegovina dated the 12th of November, 1991. I'll just display the English version of this document as the Croatian version of it is not quite so clear.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is number 118, 118A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next exhibit, Your Honour, is again a map, and it shows the areas affected by the Vance-Owen Plan and will be referred to by Professor Bianchini in the course of his evidence. I tender a copy of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is number 119.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Next, Your Honour, is a map showing parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia and indicating the main cities in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia which will be referred to in the course of Professor Bianchini's evidence. I tender that to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 120.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next bundle of documents, Your Honours, appear in both the Croatian and the English version. They consist of a series of orders and decrees made during the course of 1992 in Zagreb and, Your Honours, if these documents in this group can be tendered as one exhibit in a bundle? They will be referred to by Professor Bianchini in the course of his evidence. So perhaps they may be given one bundle number? And they're basically a series of orders during that period of 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is number 121.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps each one can be given an alphabetical listing?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 121 from "A" through "N."

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours, is a Security Council Resolution 752 of 30th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: With your permission, could you submit a copy to the Defence of document 121?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We will, Your Honours. We don't have it at the moment. We will make that available.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 122.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours, is a United Nations document, statement made by the President of the Security Council in February 1994.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honours, is an historical map of Bosnia-Herzegovina that will be referred to by Professor Bianchini in the course of his evidence relating to the movement of personnel in Bosnia during the period of the conflict, and I tender that, Your Honours. And here is the ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 124.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next exhibit is a similar exhibit of Bosnia-Herzegovina divided into three regions as denoted by the colour relating to the three groups, the Muslim population, and will be referred to again by Professor Bianchini and described by him in the course of evidence, and I tender that as the next exhibit in order.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 125.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The next exhibit, Your Honours, is a bundle of documents that we seek to tender as one exhibit, again which will be referred to by Professor Bianchini in the course of his evidence, and I would ask that they be given one exhibit number and then an alphabetical listing from "A" through to "Q," and I might just indicate the first document, "A," being the Norodni list which has an English translation attached to it and a decision on the foundation of the community of Herceg-Bosna in September 1992, letter "A." Letter "B" is a decision of the President of Croatia recognising Bosnia-Herzegovina as a sovereign independent state, dated the 7th of April, 1992. "C," Resolution 752 of the Security Council. "D," Resolution 787 of 1992, dated the 16th of November, 1992, Of the security Council of the United Nations. Declaration number 277 of the European Council, and declaration number 278, which is "E." I'm sorry, your Honour, I've just been corrected. It's not the declaration number; that is the number that appears there. The next is a United Nations document dated the 26th of April, 1993, which consists of the joint statement of the President of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Izetbegovic, and the President of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Mate Boban, witnessed by the President of Croatia, Dr. Franjo Tudjman, dated the 23rd of April, 1993. "G" is a report of the Security Council pursuant to Resolution 819 of the 30th of April, 1993. "H" is a note by the President of the Security Council of the United Nations of the 10th of May, 1993. "I" is a joint statement by the President of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic, and the President of Croatia, Dr. Franjo Tudjman, of the 17th of July, 1993. "J" is a letter dated the 27th of July, 1993, from the permanent representative of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the United Nations, addressed to the Security Council, dated the 9th of November, 1993. "K" is a letter dated the 11th of November, 1993, from the permanent representative of Bosnia-Herzegovina addressed to the President of the Security Council. "L" is a letter dated the 28th of November, 1993, from the permanent representative of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the United Nations. "M" is a letter dated the 28th of November, 1994, from the permanent representative of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the United Nations, addressed to the President of the Security Council. "N" is a letter dated the 1st of February, 1994, from the Secretary-General addressed to the President of the Security Council. "O" is a letter dated the 2nd of February, 1994, from the permanent representative of Croatia to the United Nations. "P" is a letter dated the 15th of February, 1994, from the permanent representative of Croatia to the United Nations addressed to the Security Council. "Q" is a letter dated the 17th of February, 1994, from the Secretary-General addressed to the President of the Security Council. "R" is a letter dated the 17th of February, 1994, from the permanent representative of Croatia to the United Nations addressed to the Secretary-General. "S" is a letter dated the 3rd of March, 1994, from the permanent representative of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the United Nations. And "T" is an extract of a newspaper article that will be referred to by Professor Bianchini as supporting material in the course of his evidence taken from the East European Correspondent. I don't have the date of that, but I think Professor Bianchini may assist us with a date for that. If I could tender all of those documents as one exhibit, referring to the alphabetical listing, if Your Honours please, and these are all ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So this is document 126 from "A" to "T" subject to verification.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes all the documents I have available to tender today and that will certainly be about 90 percent of the documents that need to be tendered relating to the evidence of Professor Bianchini. Professor Bianchini may have a couple of other documents that he might like to refer to in the course of his evidence which we can take care of when he's testifying, but certainly by this process, we will have reduced a very significant period of time in proceeding to tender them. As I said, Professor Bianchini will be our last witness. He still has some way to go through his evidence but, as I say, it's now been, I think, significantly reduced in time. We're sitting for half days. It's fairly hard for me to be too precise, but I think that he will take at least Tuesday and Wednesday as a minimum, and he could go over into Thursday depending on how long cross-examination may take, but certainly I'll take the best part of two of those mornings, including his evidence. As I say, we'll close our case at the end of that. We don't anticipate any other evidence that we want to call. We should be able to close our case on Thursday, I would hope, or Friday at the latest, but Thursday, I should think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, at this moment, do you have anything else to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as the defence counsel has said, we have accepted the introduction of evidence in this manner in the case in order to speed up the entire process. However, during Professor Bianchini's testimony, we hope that Professor Bianchini will comment on each one of these documents presented here -- submitted here today. If it won't be possible to discuss the document during the prosecution, then the defence in cross-examination will submit additional documents which weren't commented on in order to introduce them as evidence in the case. Otherwise, the defence has no other observations or comments. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mikulicic and also Mr. Niemann, because I believe in this manner we are going to save a great deal of time. Then we have the entire day to prepare for tomorrow and also to try to bring all this information into view that will be incorporated into the testimony of Mr. Bianchini. Do you wish to say something else, Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Very well. We are now going to then adjourn until tomorrow, but please remember that tomorrow there will be the inauguration of the second courtroom and perhaps there will be a brief break or recess around 11.00 in the morning for that inauguration. I'd like to remind Mr. Niemann, as for the translation of documents is concerned, please take into account we must have a French translation as well. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We have only prepared it in one language, but we can ask that it be prepared. I'm in the hands of the interpreters as to how long that process might take, but we can certainly make application for that to happen, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: All right. Ladies and gentlemen, we'll see you tomorrow. Good-bye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: at 10.04 a.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of May, 1998 at 9.00 a.m.
